validation.notes: Repaired packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts: migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot now skips a legacy *.jsonl when the encoded destination path already exists (existsSync(newPath) -> continue) instead of unconditionally renameSync-ing over it, so an existing destination always wins and both the destination bytes and the colliding legacy source stay untouched while the loop continues to migrate other files. The regression loads the real production module through .prale-eval/subject.mjs (real fs/path, only getAgentDir/stripBom faked) inside a workspace-local temp agent dir and asserts: (1) the pre-existing destination session keeps its exact bytes, (2) the colliding legacy source still exists with unchanged bytes, (3) no extra files appear/disappear in the destination directory, (4) an unrelated legacy session in the same run is still migrated to sessions/--work-unrelated--/ with byte-identical content, (5) a second run is likewise collision-safe and non-destructive, and (6) a fresh non-colliding session still migrates. `node --experimental-vm-modules .prale-eval/regression.mjs` exits 0 on the repaired source; replayed against an isolated copy of the original file (git HEAD, guarded only by the stale comment) it exits 1 with AssertionError 'existing destination session must win and keep its exact bytes'. The fixed and fault copies were verified locally with no network and no installed dependencies. Limitation: the repo's own vitest suite (packages/coding-agent/test/*) cannot be executed because node_modules is absent and dependency installation was not allowed, so the standalone Node regression plus the fault replay was the focused validation used.
